author: Savigny, 1809
summary: 드물게 찾아오는 길잃은새로, 전국의 하구, 간척지, 저수지 등에 국지적으로 나타난다. 분포의 대부분은 유럽과 러시아 일대이며, 여러 개발 탓에 종의 존속이 위협받고 있다.

art.subject: Eastern Imperial Eagle (Aquila heliaca), adult in winter: body and wing coverts very dark blackish-brown; crown, nape and hindneck pale golden-buff to straw-coloured, contrasting with the dark face and body; a few white feathers on the scapulars forming small white 'braces' on each side of the back; undertail coverts pale buff; flight feathers blackish; tail grey with fine dark barring and a broad black terminal band; thighs feathered dark; bill dark grey with a blackish tip and a yellow cere; dark brown eye; feet yellow.
art.scene: Korean winter estuary with reclaimed land and a reservoir nearby; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright: very large eagle with a big head and heavy hooked bill, pale golden-buff crown, nape and hindneck contrasting with the dark face and body, blackish-brown body and wing coverts, small white patches on the scapulars, square grey tail with narrow dark bars and a broad black subterminal band, long well-feathered legs

adult, in flight seen squarely from below: large head projecting well forward, long broad parallel-edged wings with fingered tips spread straight out to the sides to their full span and held flat, essentially all-dark body and underwing, grey tail with narrow dark bars and a broad black subterminal band, feet tucked under the tail
art.build: Very large, heavy eagle, a little smaller than a Golden Eagle and much smaller than a Steller's Sea Eagle, with a large head, a heavy hooked bill shorter than the head and long feathered legs. Perches upright on a tree or a mound in open country. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail fairly long and square-ended. In flight long, broad, parallel-edged wings held flat, with fingered tips; the head projects well forward.
avoid: Do not omit the small white scapular braces, and do not enlarge them into big wing patches.
Do not paint a golden-tawny nape with no white on the back; that is Golden Eagle (Aquila chrysaetos).
Do not paint a white tail or a massive yellow bill (sea eagles).
Do not paint the pale sandy, streaked plumage of the juvenile on this adult.
